pairs.subject: retry-backoff
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/resilience/detect.rs:893 The Quarantined branch of next_state releases every quarantine on a clean-run streak without consulting provenance, so an operator-forced quarantine (set_state_manual, reason recorded) is auto-lifted to Probation and its reason cleared on the transition — the breaker technique's 'only a heuristic open is probeable / never shorten a stronger open' rule is not realized, while Retired (operator-only exit) shows the provenance distinction was made for one state but not this one.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/resilience/detect.rs:893 Hysteresis breaker (Healthy/Suspect/Degraded/Quarantined/Probation as half-open), persisted, config thresholds, judged-only evidence — but quarantine exit ignores who opened it; set_state_manual(Quarantined) is lifted by detector evidence and commit_run nulls state_reason on the transition.

crates/core/src/resilience/detect.rs:182 Permanence is classified from structured status (404/410 on live uncached http only); 403/429/timeouts/DNS/cache responses never count as permanent, so rate-limited and transient failures are not misfiled.

crates/core/src/resilience/store.rs:940 By analogy: a run the fetch gate could not judge (Inconclusive/BelowCohort/ContentEmpty) consumes no ladder evidence, advances no trip count and no recovery streak — could-not-judge is spelled apart from failed.

crates/core/src/resilience/detect.rs:837 The ladder here is a ladder of states, not of delays; no attempt is rescheduled, so base/factor/cap/jitter do not apply (its stability-window idea is mirrored by recovery_runs).

crates/core/src/resilience/store.rs:217 No retry rows exist in this context; the analogous discipline (trip counts derived from persisted run rows, not an in-memory counter) is present but there is no retry-at schedule to judge.

pairs.registryProposal: circuit-breakers' decision rule 'persist breaker state with a freshness bound — discard stale' assumes the breaker gates availability of a remote dependency. For a breaker over the correctness of the system's own output (an extractor quarantine), time-based discard is wrong: a broken selector does not heal by waiting, and exit must be evidence-only. The technique should say its freshness rule applies to availability breakers, and that correctness breakers leave only on evidence.
